title: [P2-02] Stale/ambiguity/verify semantics
description:
Plan P2-02. §6.3 verification two-layer model + stale handling.

Scope:
- Observation evidence `{urlChanged?, fingerprintChanged?, valueReflected?, scrollDelta?}` vs semantic `verified: true|false|"unknown"`.
- Rules: verified:true only with action-matched evidence; click needs TARGETED evidence (element gone/aria-expanded/URL/known side-effect region) — fingerprint change alone → "unknown"; verified:false on contradicting evidence; NEVER retry mutating on "unknown".
- Stale paths: `browser.stale_snapshot`, `browser.stale_binding`, `browser.navigated`, `browser.element_not_found` mapped to ProtocolError classification (§4.2: stale_* retryable, no user action, sideEffectState none).
- TabIntent rebind rules §4.9: SW-restart auto-reconnect; Chrome restart → stale + user confirm (descriptor only suggests); ≥2 matching tabs → `browser.ambiguous_target` never auto-pick; `active_resolved` descriptor stores origin+pathPattern+titleHash+resolvedAt+originBrowserInstanceId (NO query strings/full URLs).

Tests: each verify rule; ambiguity cases; restart-scenario binding table (§4.9 four rows).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Observation vs semantic verification two-layer implemented; click needs targeted evidence.
- verified:'unknown' never triggers mutating retry.
- Stale/binding error codes match §4.2 classification (retryable flags correct).
close_reason: P2-02 done: verify.ts two-layer observation→semantic verdict wired per-step (click=targeted evidence only, unknown never retried); stale/navigated/element_not_found codes classified pre-dispatch retryable; tool-host verified passthrough + urlOriginPath nav detection; tab-binding.ts §4.9 resolver with 10 tests (SW-restart auto / Chrome-restart stale / degraded confirm / ambiguous). Commit a49f73a.

title: [P2-01] Snapshot/fingerprint/refs split
description:
Plan P2-01. Implement §6.2 two-fingerprint model + §6.4 content split.

Scope:
- `structuralFingerprint` (`sfp1:` + sha256 canonical StructuralInputs — elementCount/interactiveCount/elements{role,name,tag,type,boundsBucket}/framePathSignature) for ref validity; `stateFingerprint` (`tfp1:` + sha256 StateInputs incl. urlOriginPath/readyState/scrollBucket/fieldValueHashes/checkedRoles) for verify.
- Field hashes: `HMAC-SHA256(salt, canonical({tabOrigin,ref,value}))` truncated 16 bytes → base64url; salt per-install in `chrome.storage.local` with `setAccessLevel TRUSTED_CONTEXTS` if available; `saltEpoch` incremented on salt change; password/payment ALWAYS `"[redacted]"` never hashed; no plaintext field values persisted anywhere.
- `fieldIdentity = sha256(structuralPath|role|name|type|formIndex)`; unresolvable → `verified:"unknown"`.
- `snapshotId="snap:"+ulid`, TTL 5min, LRU 32/task; stale rules: structural change/tab close/navigation/TTL — NOT stateFingerprint change.
- Content split §6.4: `content/{snapshot,actions,refs,verify,transport}.ts` extracted from `content/index.ts` (2566 lines) — keep behavior, regression test BEFORE split.
- `BrowserSnapshot`/`BrowserElement` types from [P0-02]; caps from config `snapshot.maxElements=80, maxTextChars=12000`.

Tests: fingerprint stability (typing doesn't stale refs), state change detection, salt epoch invalidation, redaction guarantees, ref resolution + ambiguity (`browser.ambiguous_target`), content-split regression suite.

## Acceptance Criteria
- structuralFingerprint/stateFingerprint implemented per §6.2 with salt+saltEpoch+fieldIdentity rules.
- No plaintext field values anywhere; password/payment always redacted.
- Content split done with pre-split regression suite green.
- snapshotId TTL/LRU per spec.
close_reason: P2-01 done: sfp1/tfp1 fingerprints + HMAC field hashes + redaction, SnapshotRegistry TTL/LRU/tab-invalidation, stale_snapshot enforcement, content split into refs/snapshot/actions/verify/transport. 15 shared + 10 tool-host + 4 salt tests; 974 extension tests pass (2 pre-existing unrelated failures). title: [GateA-A3] Sign off identity model shape
description:

- Privacy-first registration §6.1.1: register sends NO tab list/URLs/titles; `browser.tabs.list` on demand; internal pages excluded.
- IDs are namespace, not security identity (§3.4.3 threat model).

Deliverable: sign-off on shape; mark mechanism `PROVISIONAL(spike-B6)`.

- Mechanism explicitly marked PROVISIONAL(spike-B6).

title: [P1-01] Gateway skeleton: in-memory store + lock + IPC + hello/auth
description:

- `lock.ts`: OS advisory lock — POSIX `flock`, Windows `LockFileEx`; metadata `{pid, startedAt(OS), execPath, fence(ULID)}` written through the locked fd + fsync; NO mtime reclaim, NO unlink-while-held; reclaim only via lock acquisition → bump fence.

title: [GateA-A2] Sign off two-lock ownership + crash table
description:
Gate A item A2. Sign off Gateway startup/ownership contract §3.3.1–§3.3.3 + §5.1 startup order.

Key semantics to confirm:
- TWO locks: `gateway.start.lock` (native host/CLI, short-lived, serializes spawn) and `gateway.lock` (Gateway lifetime). No process owns both simultaneously; overlap during handoff is allowed BY DESIGN.
- Ownership = OS advisory lock: POSIX `flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)`, Windows `LockFileEx`. OS releases on death. **mtime-based reclaim is FORBIDDEN** (suspended process >10s must NOT be reclaimed).
- Fencing token (ULID, monotonic) in lock metadata; every state write/endpoint/hello must match current fence; mismatch → refuse + self-shutdown. Reclaim = acquire OS lock → bump fence → publish.
- Crash table §3.3.2 rows 1–7 + 5a/5a′/5b: ping failure ≠ dead; only PID+start-time+execPath proof allows reclaim; alive-but-unresponsive → `gateway.unresponsive`, never spawn second Gateway.
- Startup order §5.1: lock → config → store+migrate → RECOVERY SCAN+COMMIT → providers/browser/sessions → IPC listen (returns `gateway.starting` for non-hello) → atomic endpoint publish → ready.
- `startedAt` = OS process start time (kernelStartTime if available), not app write time.

title: [Spike-B5] IPC transport spike: named pipe ACL vs TCP+token
description:
Gate B spike B5 — REQUIRED before locking IPC transport (plan §3.4.1–§3.4.3). Blocks Gate A-final.

Candidate transports:
- Windows: Named pipe `\\.\pipe\chromex-gw-<sha256(userSid+dataDir)[:16]>` — no TCP, user-scoped, no firewall prompt.
- macOS/Linux: Unix domain socket in `0700` dir.
- Fallback: `127.0.0.1` + random port + opaque token file.

Mandatory spike tests (pass/fail criteria):
1. User A creates gateway; User B connects → B rejected (the real security goal).
2. Same-user process without token → behavior documented (not a goal; must not crash, must log clearly).
3. Gateway restart with stale pipe → no cross-connection confusion; endpoint recreated.
4. Two Chrome profiles same user → both connect, `profileId` separates.
5. Node `net.createServer(pipe)` on Windows with explicit ACL → prove ACL control possible or document limits.

Decision rule: if test 1 fails with default Node APIs and no native module → choose TCP+token as default, do not force pipe.

Also produce threat model §3.4.3 sign-off: pipe/ACL/token defend against OTHER USERS only; same-user malware can read token file; cannot identify "real Chrome Native Host" in MVP.

Deliverables: `scripts/spike/ipc-*` tests + ADR `docs/adr/ipc-transport.md` + config `gateway.ipc.transport: auto|pipe|tcp|unix` semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 5 spike tests executed with recorded pass/fail.
- ADR docs/adr/ipc-transport.md picks transport per decision rule (pipe only if user-isolation proven; else TCP+token).
- Threat model §3.4.3 signed (other-user defense only, no same-user malware claim).
